issues.reason: The oblique rule pins the head to the preposition actually used - 'in stays In; During renders only the word during' - so the framing PP 'in trading' must be (In sk_close_1 sk_trade_1), not a near-fit synonym head.

This mistakes the reviewer's own registered gap (a bare differential with no stated standard) for a defect: the atom is true of 'up 64 cents' and well-typed in Measure's open-class scale slot, and price and increase are two different scales, so they are not competing values of one dimension.

Nothing in the instruction set restricts Measure's bearer to non-events (it rides event witnesses for duration), and moving the price onto the stock would assert a standing price the sentence never claims - the event-anchored form is the conservative reading inside the reviewer's own time-indexed-value gap.

gaps_confirmed: a bare differential with no stated standard ('up 64 cents') - MoreBy needs both relata and the prior close is never mentioned
no slot for the time at which a value held ('closed Wednesday at $23.40') - Measure carries no time index, so the price must ride either the entity or the event
new_gaps: currency has no seeded canonical unit or conversion factor, so the dollar and cent measures on this one event cannot be compared or combined
repair_summary: Replaced the synonym head (During sk_close_1 sk_trade_1) with the surface preposition (In sk_close_1 sk_trade_1), renaming its proof name close_during to close_in; nothing else changed.
notes: The third gap claim is refuted rather than confirmed - a framing PP over an event-noun is covered, by the preposition-named oblique taking the surface head. (Past sk_trade_1) on the framing adjunct was left alone: it is true, and the 'class atom and ordering relation and nothing else' restriction is stated only for temporal before/after anchors.
